descriptionChirho: The proper noun Sibmah (also spelled Sivmah, Sebam), a Moabite town famous for its vineyards, mentioned in the tribal allotment narratives (Num 32:3, Josh 13:19) and in prophetic oracles against Moab (Isa 16:8-9, Jer 48:32). All three sense clusters are purely grammatical variants: the base form (4x), conjunctive 'and-Sivmah' (1x), and conjunctive 'and-Sebam' (1x). Multilingual evidence uniformly points to a single place: Spanish 'Sibma/Seban,' Arabic 'sibma/sabam,' Hindi 'sibma/sebam,' Korean 'sibeu-ma/sebae,' Swahili 'Sibma/Sebamu.' The spelling variation Sebam (Num 32:3) versus Sibmah (Num 32:38) likely reflects dialectal or scribal variation for the same location.
